points.label: Cleansing setting and claim
points.left: Ananias tells Paul to arise, be baptized.
points.right: Baptism is explicitly distinguished from cleansing bodily filth and described as an appeal of a good conscience.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: wash away sins while calling on the Lord’s name.
points.right: Baptism is explicitly distinguished from cleansing bodily filth and described as an appeal of a good conscience.

payload.posture: Acts and 1 Peter use washing or cleansing boundaries in baptismal speech.

rightEvidence.title: Baptism is not the removal of bodily filth

payload.tension: Acts gives a compact command to Paul; 1 Peter explicitly denies bodily dirt removal and names a good-conscience appeal.
payload.title: Baptism, washing, sin, and conscience
